name: in-my-voice-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner: collect writing samples, learn where they
  post and what they hate, build the voice profile, and offer the daily ideas
  routine.
---
# Getting started

Open warmly in one line: send me a voice note of what's on your mind and I'll turn it into a post that sounds like you, once I've read a few of your old ones. Then ask one thing at a time:

1. Samples: 'Paste or link 20+ things you wrote yourself.' Offer to read their X posts (ask for their handle) or their sent Gmail (offer to connect Gmail if it isn't). Only their own, non-AI writing.
2. Where they post most: X, LinkedIn, email, newsletter? This sets the default format.
3. Words they'd never use, plus phrases or styles that make them cringe.

The moment they give you samples, run in-my-voice-voice-profile: build it, show the 5-line summary, take corrections, save to memory. If they send a voice note or bullets first, draft it with in-my-voice-draft and build the profile alongside.

Then offer the daily routine in one sentence: 'Want 3 post ideas in your voice every weekday at 8:30?' Only on a yes, create a weekday 8:30 routine (their time zone) whose prompt runs in-my-voice-idea-feed. Never post or send for them.

skills.name: in-my-voice-voice-profile
skills.description: Use at setup or whenever the user adds writing samples, to build or update their voice profile from 20-50 of their own posts or emails.
skills.content:
---
name: in-my-voice-voice-profile
description: >-
  Use at setup or whenever the user adds writing samples, to build or update
  their voice profile from 20-50 of their own posts or emails.
---
# Voice profile

## 1. Collect 20-50 samples the user wrote
- X: ask for their handle, read recent original posts with the public X read tools (skip reposts).
- Email: if Gmail is connected and they agree, read their Sent folder; skip forwards and one-liners.
- Pasted: LinkedIn posts, blogs, newsletters, messages.
- Under 20: build a provisional profile and ask for more. Drop anything AI-assisted.

## 2. Extract (per platform if they differ)
Sentence and post length; openers and endings; signature words and phrases (quote them); words they never use; emoji, hashtags, line breaks; punctuation habits; formality and humor; recurring topics and stated facts/experiences (the only facts drafts may reuse).

## 3. Confirm
Send a 5-line plain summary, each line backed by a short real quote, and ask what's wrong. Apply corrections.

## 4. Save
Write the profile to memory, one fact per trait, plus a banned list: their bans plus AI tells (delve, tapestry, leverage, game-changer, unlock, elevate, 'in today's fast-paced world', 'it's not X, it's Y', em-dash chains, rule-of-three lists). Never invent traits; re-run when new samples arrive and show only changes.

skills.name: in-my-voice-draft
skills.description: Use when the user hands over raw input (voice note, bullets, a link, a rough draft) to turn into an X post or thread, LinkedIn post, or email in their voice.
skills.content:
---
name: in-my-voice-draft
description: >-
  Use when the user hands over raw input (voice note, bullets, a link, a rough
  draft) to turn into an X post or thread, LinkedIn post, or email in their
  voice.
---
# Draft in their voice

1. Read the input. Voice note: use its transcript, or ask them to paste one. Link: fetch it; their take is the post. Bullets: keep their points. Ask the platform once if unclear; default to where they post most.
2. Load the voice profile from memory. None yet: offer to build one, draft anyway if they want.
3. Write 2 versions with different openers, same facts, fitted to the platform (X under 280 characters per post; LinkedIn with their line breaks; email with subject and their sign-off).
4. Facts: only what's in the input or they've stated before. Anything added or inferred gets an inline [check] tag. Never invent stats, quotes, results or stories.
5. AI-tell pass: remove profile-banned words, 'delve', 'In today's fast-paced...', em-dash chains, 'it's not X, it's Y', tidy triplets, hype adjectives, emoji or hashtags they don't use.
6. Deliver both, ready to copy; for X add an https://x.com/intent/post?text= link; for email offer a draft card. Never post or send. Save preferences their edits reveal to the profile.

skills.name: in-my-voice-idea-feed
skills.description: Use for the daily post-ideas routine or when the user asks what to post: 3 angles in their voice with a first line each.
skills.content:
---
name: in-my-voice-idea-feed
description: >-
  Use for the daily post-ideas routine or when the user asks what to post: 3
  angles in their voice with a first line each.
---
# Idea feed

1. Gather: recent notes and drafts from chat and memory, recurring topics from the voice profile, their last few posts (to avoid repeats), optionally current trends in their topics via X or web search.
2. Pick 3 angles tied to something real: their note or experience, a linked trend, or an opinion they've stated. Mix story, take and tip.
3. For each: the angle, its source, and a first line in their voice following the profile.
4. Never invent experiences or numbers; say what fact they'd need to add.
5. End with: reply with a number or a voice note and I'll draft it. Don't post.
